headline: Meta launches Ray-Ban Meta Audio smart glasses without cameras
summary: Meta's new smart glasses ditch cameras for audio features and AI access, shipping October 13th starting at $349.
details: Meta has announced the Ray-Ban Meta Audio, its first smart glasses that completely remove cameras, focusing instead on audio capabilities and AI integration. This move comes as the company aims to address privacy concerns and cater to user preference for audio features.

The new glasses are designed to offer a more discreet experience, allowing users to take calls, respond to messages via voice, and stream music or podcasts without being disconnected from their surroundings. They also provide access to Meta AI for real-time translation and information retrieval.

Ditching the cameras results in a lighter design, weighing 43 grams, compared to Meta's previous camera-equipped models which range from 49.2 to 69 grams. The Ray-Ban Meta Audio also boasts an impressive battery life, offering up to 12 hours on a single charge, with an additional 48 hours provided by the charging case.

Meta has also focused on comfort and customization, incorporating the same fit adjustments as previous models, including adjustable temple tips, customizable nose pads, and spring-loaded hinges. The glasses are available in two new styles, Burbank and Clubmaster, with 23 color and lens combinations, and support for prescription lenses.

While Meta frames this as an evolution of its smart glasses, the removal of cameras is a significant step in addressing public perception and privacy concerns associated with its previous camera-enabled devices.
The Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses are available for pre-order starting today at $349 and are scheduled to ship on October 13th.

topic: youtube enhances creator tools with ai-powered video A/B testing and custom feeds
headline_marked: YouTube launches [[video A/B testing]] and custom feeds
headline: YouTube launches video A/B testing and custom feeds
summary: Creators can now test different video cuts, while users gain control over their front page recommendations.
details: YouTube is rolling out significant upgrades for creators and viewers alike. The platform is introducing A/B testing for video cuts, allowing creators to test up to three different versions of a video to see which performs best. This feature expands on existing A/B testing for thumbnails and titles.

Creators will also benefit from new AI-powered feedback tools within YouTube Studio. These tools offer personalized advice on pacing, storytelling, and structure, potentially assisting creators in generating new video cuts with greater ease.

For viewers, YouTube is finally introducing custom feeds. This feature aims to give users more control over their recommendations, addressing frustrations with irrelevant content cluttering their front page and potentially revitalizing engagement on the platform.

The platform is also enhancing discovery for podcasts with a new feature coming to YouTube Music. These updates were announced at YouTube's Made on YouTube event for creators, signaling a major push towards improving user experience and creator tools.
